facts.text: Over-fitting occurs when a system's settings are adjusted so closely to its tuning tests that the system performs well on those tests but worse on new tests.
facts.quote: Over-fitting is what happens when a system's settings are adjusted so closely to the particular tests it was tuned on that it performs well on those tests and worse on anything new.

facts.text: The braking system's tuned quantities are detection thresholds, zone sizes, confirmation filters and timing constants.
facts.quote: For the braking system, the tuned quantities are detection thresholds, zone sizes, confirmation filters and timing constants.

facts.text: Adjusting braking-system settings until every tuning scenario passes makes those scenarios a measure of fit to the settings rather than an independent performance measure.
facts.quote: If engineers adjust them until every tuning scenario passes, the tuning scenarios no longer measure anything; they measure how well the settings fit themselves.

facts.text: Braking-system tuning should use grouped partitions rather than random frame splits, holding out entire sites, weather episodes, machine identities or scenario families; adjacent frames from one run in both tuning and validation sets create severe leakage.
facts.quote: Use grouped partitions, not random frame splits: hold out entire sites, weather episodes, machine identities or scenario families, because adjacent frames from the same run appearing in both tuning and validation sets create severe leakage.

facts.text: Braking-system tuning should maintain three separate datasets: a development or tuning set, a validation or confirmation set, and an untouched audit set.
facts.quote: Keep a three-way split: a development or tuning set, a validation or confirmation set, and an untouched audit set.

facts.text: Braking-system tuning should use leave-one-site-type-out validation to test generalization to unseen sites.
facts.quote: Use leave-one-site-type-out validation to test generalization to unseen sites.

facts.text: The frozen test set for braking-system tuning should have limited query frequency, be frozen at a version, and be refreshed only for a new release.
facts.quote: Limit how often the frozen set is queried, freezing it at a version and refreshing it only for a new release.

facts.text: Braking-system tuning should report tuned-set and frozen-set performance side by side; a large performance gap signals over-fitting.
facts.quote: Report tuned-set and frozen-set performance side by side; a large gap signals over-fitting [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Over-fitting to the simulator is a project failure mode in which virtual metrics keep improving while performance on held-out real data stalls or worsens.
facts.quote: Chapter 13 describes "the function is overfitted to the simulator" as a project failure mode: virtual metrics keep improving while performance on held-out real data stalls or worsens.

facts.text: The recommended remedy for over-fitting to the simulator is independent withheld physical datasets and blind correlation tests.
facts.quote: The remedy is independent withheld physical datasets and blind correlation tests [Chapter 13].

facts.text: Physics-based parameterization has low over-fitting risk when its inputs are measured independently.
facts.quote: low for physics-based parameterization whose inputs are measured independently

facts.text: Evolutionary and cost-weighted optimization have higher over-fitting risk because many configurations are tried.
facts.quote: higher for evolutionary and cost-weighted optimization because many configurations are tried

facts.text: Direct per-model manual tuning is susceptible to engineer and test-set over-fit and recreates the historical multi-year problem.
facts.quote: direct per-model manual tuning is described as susceptible to engineer and test-set over-fit and as recreating "the historical multi-year problem" [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Over-fitting is the central danger of braking-system tuning under time pressure because a system that passes every known test looks finished.
facts.quote: Over-fitting is the central danger of tuning under time pressure, because a system that passes every known test looks finished.

facts.text: Protection against braking-system over-fitting should include a frozen, pre-registered audit set that the tuning team cannot inspect case by case.
facts.quote: a frozen, pre-registered audit set that the tuning team cannot see case by case

facts.text: Protection against braking-system over-fitting should use physics-based parameters that are measured rather than fitted.
facts.quote: physics-based parameters that are measured rather than fitted [Chapter 9].
